article_title: Children's English Reading Story Generation via Supervised Fine-Tuning of Compact LLMs with Controllable Difficulty and Safety
citation: Qian Shen, Fanghua Cao, Min Yao, Shlok Gilda, Bonnie J. Dorr, Walter L. Leite. (2026). Children's English Reading Story Generation via Supervised Fine-Tuning of Compact LLMs with Controllable Difficulty and Safety. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.13709v1
title: QLoRA-based SFT pipeline for phoneme-controlled children's story generation with three 8B LLMs and four experimental designs
description: The article builds a pipeline that fine-tunes Llama 3 8B, Apertus 8B-instruct-2509, and Granite 3.3 8b-instruct using QLoRA (4-bit NF4 quantization with LoRA adapters, rank 32, alpha 64) on input-target pairs pairing curriculum lesson phonemes with 2,580 stories generated zero-shot by GPT-4o and Llama 3.3 70B from the 129-lesson UFLI K-2 curriculum. Four designs are compared: baseline SFT, "Good Stories" quality filtering (996 stories selected), Rewarded SFT with reward-weighted loss, and SFT with simulated children's reading errors generated by GPT-OSS-120B. Evaluation uses Spache readability, LM-PPL, coherence, syntactic complexity, toxicity, and Self-BLEU.
requirements: Training data derived from an expert-designed K-2 phonics curriculum specifying target phonemes per lesson
Sufficient stories per lesson as SFT targets (2,580 stories, 50-350 words each)
constraints: Computational resources limited to three L4 GPUs, preventing some SFT strategies and constraining hyperparameters such as training epochs
Sample size was insufficient for a full RLHF pipeline
Only a single expert-designed curriculum and one language were used
target_learners: Children in kindergarten through 2nd grade learning English reading
target_learning_goals: Oral reading fluency through engaging level-appropriate stories
examples: Rewarded SFT assigned each training example a scalar reward computed as the unweighted average of five normalized automatic metrics, reweighting the standard cross-entropy loss

citation: Owsley Cynthia. (2012). Visual Processing Speed. Vision Research. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.visres.2012.11.014
title: UFOV test software (Visual Awareness Research Group)
description: A commercially available personal-computer software version of the useful field of view test, usable with a touch-screen or mouse, with four subtests measuring minimum stimulus duration thresholds for correct central task performance. The review states "The UFOV® test is also briefer than the original version, and can be completed in ≤ 15 minutes", with thresholds ranging from 16.67 to 500 ms. It agrees well with the original test version (0.658 to 0.746) and shows test-retest reliability estimated between .735 and .884 depending on response modality.
requirements: A personal computer with a touch-screen or mouse for administration
constraints: Peripheral targets are presented at ~10° eccentricity only, not at the further eccentricities of the original test
target_learning_goals: assessment of visual processing speed, divided attention, and selective attention
examples: The original version took up to 30 minutes to administer; the software version's fourth subtest makes central target discrimination more difficult
key_sources: Owsley Cynthia. (2012). Visual Processing Speed. Vision Research. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.visres.2012.11.014
